key_insight: Enhanced state features and reward shaping improve deep reinforcement learning flow control across synthetic jet positions, achieving 8%–34% drag reduction at Reynolds numbers of 100–400.
engineering_relevance: More adaptive synthetic jet control could reduce drag, lift fluctuations, vortex shedding, and actuation energy across varying flow conditions.
method: Train deep reinforcement learning controllers for multiple synthetic jet positions and Reynolds numbers.
Enhance dynamic state features to improve flow-state representation.
Reshape rewards to balance aerodynamic performance and energy consumption.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 8%–34% drag reduction over Reynolds numbers of 100–400 and improved control across tested jet positions.
watch_item: Performance beyond the tested Reynolds-number range and transfer to physical systems remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Toward fully stabilized flow control using deep reinforcement learning
